author: Dale Roberts
title: OK, OK, I know this is just a short term event, but it's wor
text:
OK, OK, I know this is just a short term event, but it's worth reporting just the same. Keep in mind that I purchased these 15 Achievers for the potential of an outperformance through a market correction, but I'd certainly take some outperformance along that path to the next major market correction. And who knows, maybe we'll soon get to test out theses Achievers and the Achievers Index ETF ( VIG ) in a real market meltdown. 
Those 15 holdings are Nike (NYSE: NKE ), CVS (NYSE: CVS ), Walgreens (NASDAQ: WBA ), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ), 3M (NYSE: MMM ), Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE: CL ), Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ ), Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ), Medtronic (NYSE: MDT ), Abbott (NYSE: ABT ), PepsiCo (NYSE: PEP ), Texas Instruments (NYSE: TXN ), Walmart (NYSE: WMT ), United Technologies (NYSE: UTX ) and Lowe's (NYSE: LOW ). 
Here's the returns history of those 15 Dividend Achievers, as Portfolio 1, vs. the Vanguard Index ETF. The period is March of 2015 through to end of January 2018. As always past performance does not guarantee future returns. The portfolio is rebalanced on an annual schedule.

We see some slight total return alpha. Some of that alpha is courtesy of the rebalancing effort. Some of the underperformers have started to deliver on the share price appreciation front. The version of the portfolio without rebalaning would have returned a 12.07% CAGR. And some of the alpha is created by me ignoring the financial filters of the index. While Wal-Mart and Qualcomm were removed from the index, I continued to hold and add to those positions. Those index rejects have recently outpeformed the total index. Here's my article Looks Like That Smart Beta Just Got Dummer and Dummer. 
Here are the returns of the companies from March of 2015 to end of January 2018. For the period VIG has a CAGR of 11.71%.

And back to the turnaround for some of the 'losers' in the portfolio, here are the returns from January of 2017 to end of January 2018. Again Portfolio 1 is those 15 Dividend Achievers.

And here are the individual company returns for the period. VIG returned 25.91% for the period. Of course, Qualcomm's outperformance is more recent as it now the target of a takeover offer. What investor or smart beta filter could have seen that coming?
I am now down to two drastic underperformers with my healthcare retail duopoly of CVS and Walgreens. Of course, I will stick by those two names as well. Many investors like an investment theme that ends in "opoly". I hope I can write one day on the recovery of those two names. They certainly reside in the wonderful sector of healthcare ( XLV ) where the long term trends are favourable due to the again populations and rising healthcare needs. 
When I first did my study of index skimming, I wrote that I would be comfortable skimming 20-25 names in the attempt to replicate the index performance. My readers will know that I also hold 3 US stock "picks" by way of Apple ( AAPL ), BlackRock ( BLK ) and Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.B ). Given that, I decided at the time to stick with 15 Achievers and my 3 picks.
When I add in those 3 picks at the approximate portfolio weightings, I see some exaggerated alpha. The period is January of 2017 to end of January 2018. The recent performance is impressive, but the alpha from beginning of 2015 is just above 1.6% compared to the VIG benchmark. The mix just slightly outperforms the S&P 500 ( IVV ) for that period.
The main takeaways from this real life, real monies exercise (yes our retirement prospects will be affected), that it did not take many companies to replicate the index and that consistency and perseverance has paid off. I 'bought em' without additional research beyond the index construct, and I continue to add without looking. Well, I'll admit I look to see what companies need some love, need some monies to top 'em up. In the attempt to rebalance on the fly, I add monies to the companies that are at a lesser portfolio value; I let the winners run. Of course, portfolio rebalancing can be known as a form of value investing ( RPV ), as we are often buying more current earnings when those companies are down in price. Of course, those companies might be out of market favour and there is certainly no guarantee that those companies will perform to the satisfaction of the market makers and that the share prices will recover.
Another consideration and observation would be that I trusted professional portfolio analysis and construction for original purchase of my Dividend Achievers holdings. I did not pretend to be Warren Buffett or a team of CPAs and mathematicians. I trusted professional experience and knowledge for the portfolio selections. I am now certainly trusting sloth like, hands off patience and consistency in the ongoing portfolio maintenance.
When individual investors report on their progress, we almost exclusively see underperformance to simple indices. That's not surprising. As an investor, do you want to take your cues from professional portfolio construction or from those who demonstrate an ability to deliver negative alpha? In this modern age of investing, ETFs and indices allow us to look under the hood to see the companies that are found by certain factors. An investor can certainly buy the ETF version, or look to the individual index holdings for portfolio candidates. Thank you very much, but I'll go for the winners vs. the losers.
Of course that's the advice given by Warren Buffett who suggests retail investors simply buy the S&P 500 or other indices in a very cost effective manner. 
And once again, maybe my 15 Dividend Achievers will get the call and get the chance to prove their mettle in a real market meltdown. Nobody knows what will happen on that front, but Mr. Market or Mr. Volatility has certainly given us a little warning shot to the ribs. I call it a little love tap. It might be an opportunity for investors to take stock, or let's say take stock of "how much" stocks they might be holding. Here's my recent article Mr. Volatility is Asking You, Taunting You - So Do You Wanna Go? 
Does your investment plan include a major market meltdown that could last months or years? From that article and from Mr. Mike Tyson ...
Everyone has a plan until I punch them in the face.
Are you ready to get punched in the face? I hope my Dividend Achievers and bond allocation are up to the task. 
Thanks for reading. Please always know and invest within your risk tolerance level. Always know and understand all tax implications and consequences.
Happy Investing.
Dale
